docs.text: high court ruling that senator gallagher was ineligible to be elected at the 2016 election under section 44(i) of the constitution (re gallagher) senator gallagher was a british citizen by descent. she signed a declaration of renunciation on 20 april 2016, lodged with the united kingdom home office on 26 april 2016, but the home office did not register the renunciation until 16 august 2016, after nominations for the 2 july 2016 election had closed. on 6 december 2017, at her request, the senate referred questions about her eligibility to the court of disputed returns. on 9 may 2018 the high court unanimously held that she was a citizen of a foreign power when nominated and was therefore incapable of being chosen as a senator under section 44(i), and that the exception for cases where foreign law irremediably prevents renunciation did not apply. the vacancy was filled by a special count and she returned to the senate at the 2019 election. a section 44 ineligibility finding concerns constitutional eligibility; the court made no finding about her honesty or conduct. high court of australia sitting as the court of disputed returns, on a reference from the senate court's answers: whether section 44(i) created a vacancy, 'yes'; how it should be filled, 'by a special count of the ballot papers'. the parliament of australia records her 2016 election as 'ruled void 9.5.2018 under section 44 (i) of the constitution'. she was elected again at the 2019 election. 2017-12-06 6 december 2017 katy gallagher australian labor party official finding

docs.text: termination of mr hastie's standby army reserve service after he declined a defence request to remove images of himself in uniform from 2016 election material during the 2016 federal election campaign, defence asked mr hastie, then the member for canning and a member of the standby army reserve, to remove images of himself in uniform from campaign material, citing policy that australian defence force members not engage in political activity in uniform without approval. mr hastie declined, saying the image reflected his personal and professional history and that as a former officer he was no longer under military authority. the army issued a notice of intention to terminate his service for failing to comply with directions and defence policy, and his reserve service was terminated. australian army / department of defence department of defence statement, as quoted by the abc on 9 june 2016: 'defence contacted mr hastie, a member of the standby army reserve, and requested he remove imagery of himself in uniform from election campaign material. regrettably, mr hastie did not comply with this request. accordingly, the army issued mr hastie with a notice indicating the intention to terminate his service because he had failed to comply with directions and defence policy.' 2016-06-09 9 june 2016 andrew hastie liberal party of australia official finding

docs.text: queensland prosecution over the 1997 registration of pauline hanson's one nation: convictions quashed and acquittals entered in october 1997 ms hanson applied to register pauline hanson's one nation as a queensland political party on the basis that it had more than 500 members. after a civil challenge, the supreme court of queensland set the registration aside in august 1999, finding the electoral commissioner's decision had been induced by fraud or misrepresentation. following a police investigation, ms hanson and david ettridge were charged in july 2001 with dishonestly inducing the registration, and ms hanson was also charged with dishonestly obtaining electoral reimbursements. a district court jury convicted both on 20 august 2003 and each was sentenced to three years' imprisonment. on 6 november 2003 the queensland court of appeal quashed the convictions, set aside the sentences and directed that verdicts of acquittal be entered. a crime and misconduct commission inquiry requested by the queensland parliament found in january 2004 that no misconduct or impropriety was associated with the litigation or the police investigation. supreme court of queensland; queensland police service; queensland director of public prosecutions; district court of queensland; queensland court of appeal; crime and misconduct commission (queensland) convictions quashed; verdicts of acquittal entered (queensland court of appeal, 6 november 2003). no conviction stands. the crime and misconduct commission (january 2004) found that 'no misconduct or other impropriety has been shown to have been associated with the conduct of the litigation concerning ms hanson and mr ettridge, or with the police investigations leading to the prosecution'. 1998-07-10 10 july 1998 pauline hanson one nation overturned / appealed
